clue.text: Vigilante, say, turned off news about noisy dispute

indicators.note: one word placed about another wraps round it, so the dispute goes inside

parts.note: someone turned off by something is bored by it
a row is a loud quarrel
word can mean news, as in 'any word from him?'

explanation.surface: A news report on a heated argument over a vigilante, which bored the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigilante comes into English from Spanish, so it is an example of a loanword taken from another language.

clue.text: Being inferior, 20 succeeded in 24s

parts.note: the answer to 20 down is NOUGHT, which is zero, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: the succession abbreviation sits in the other word, placed inside it

parts.note: the answer to 24 across is TRADING POST; such posts in frontier country were forts
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced clue: being second-rate, zero followed up in a string of outposts.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 down needs its crossers: 20 down (NOUGHT, giving O) and 24 across (TRADING POST, whose plural suggests FORTS).
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as 'of sorts' is a poor or makeshift example, so the phrase means being inferior or second-rate.

clue.text: Notice that repairs are on the way

definitions.text: Notice that repairs are on the way

parts.words: Notice that repairs are on the way
parts.note: reads as a promise that fixing is coming soon, but 'the way' is the road itself, being dug up for work

explanation.surface: An announcement promising that repair work will soon arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'road up' sign is a British warning notice placed where roadworks are under way on the carriageway.

clue.text: Excluding considerable influences wouldn't make you this mean

definitions.text: Excluding considerable influences wouldn't make you this mean

parts.words: Excluding considerable influences wouldn't make you this mean
parts.note: reads like moral advice about being stingy, but 'mean' is a statistical average in which heavier items count for more

explanation.surface: Advice that ignoring powerful people won't make you a nasty person.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics, this kind of average multiplies each value by a factor reflecting its importance, so large influences are included, not left out.

clue.text: I needed to read it in this original form

definitions.text: I needed to read it in this original form

indicators.note: the clue's words are to be rearranged into a different form; 'original' suggests making something new of them

explanation.surface: A reader insisting on a printed paper rather than the screen version.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the anagram indicator 'in this original form' also describes the printed newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead-tree edition is a jokey name for the paper version of a publication, printed on pulp from felled trees, its original medium.

clue.text: In character, unveiled egg dish

indicators.note: the covering at each end is stripped off, so the outer letters of the combined word go

parts.note: being at home means being in
a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: An egg dish revealed, apparently stripped bare while in character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In character' looks like a phrase about acting, but each word is a piece. 'Unveiled' removes the H and R at the ends of HOMELETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: This is beaten eggs cooked flat in a pan, often folded over a filling, a classic egg-based dish.

clue.text: Receiving one doddery old PM with a certificate

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take in the numeral, which sits inside them
doddery means shaky and unsteady, so these letters are set tottering into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An elderly, shaky former prime minister receives a certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doddery' rearranges OLD PM to DPLOM; 'Receiving' puts I after its D.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a document awarded on completing a course, a formal certificate of qualification.

clue.text: The final stage in hand

parts.note: being at home means being in
a straight is a poker hand of five cards in sequence

explanation.surface: Suggests the last phase of a task is well under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hand' reads as an idiom meaning under control, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straight stretch of a racecourse before the finish, used figuratively for the closing phase of any undertaking.

clue.text: Capital cuts inaccurately give us a projection

indicators.note: the capital cuts into the other letters, going inside them
putting the words down inaccurately means getting their letters out of order

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: A complaint that badly made budget reductions in a capital city give us a distorted forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inaccurately' rearranges GIVE US A to VISUAGE; 'cuts' puts LIMA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A projection is a picture thrown onto a screen or formed in the mind, a mental or optical image seen by the eye.

clue.text: Who might resort to violence when smuggling gold?

definitions.text: Who might resort to violence when smuggling gold?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters carry the gold hidden inside them
read as re-sort, the letters are sorted again into a new order

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Asks what kind of person turns violent while running contraband gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is definition and wordplay. 'Resort' rearranges TO VIOLENCE and 'when smuggling' puts OR inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Godfather's mafia boss is a fictional crime lord willing to use force while running illegal rackets.

clue.text: Quite like battery acid, this soup?

definitions.text: Quite like battery acid, this soup?

parts.words: Quite like battery acid, this soup?
parts.note: reads as a complaint about a sour broth, but battery acid has an acidity reading near zero on the pH scale, written pH 0

explanation.surface: A diner grumbling that the soup tastes as sharp as battery acid.
explanation.walkthrough: pH measures acidity and strong acids sit near 0; written as pH 0 the reading looks like the soup's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup made with broth, rice noodles and herbs.

clue.text: Cyrano found fame this costly!

definitions.meaning: Cyrano de Bergerac, the swordsman-poet of Rostand's play, is famous because of his huge nose
paying ... means paying far too much

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being overcharged, while Cyrano owes his fame to his enormous nose.

clue.text: See 11
What you should do if you don't know about opening keg

indicators.note: the abbreviation opens the word, coming at its start

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

parts.words: What you should do if you don't know
parts.note: if you don't know something, you should ask

explanation.surface: Advice for someone puzzled about how to open a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The long phrase looks like the definition but supplies the verb; the definition is just 'keg'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask is a barrel for liquids such as beer or wine, the same container as a keg.

clue.text: What present onset of Christmastide will become with a little time?

definitions.text: What present onset of Christmastide will become with a little time?

indicators.note: the letters will become something else, rearranged into a new order
the onset of a word is its first letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A reflection on how today's Christmas build-up will soon be history.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is definition and wordplay: 'will become' rearranges PRESENT with C and A to RECENTPAS, and T ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Once a little time passes, what is happening now becomes something that happened lately, the period just gone.

clue.text: Chopin, Paderewski et al rating director

parts.note: the composer Chopin and the pianist-statesman Paderewski were both Poles
a rating is an ordinary sailor, and tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Ranks Polish pianists, as if assessing which is the leading star performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog also allows POLE + STAR (rating as in star rating); either way the pieces join the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris guides navigators by marking north, so it serves as a guide or director.

clue.text: Tipsy cakes go for a song

indicators.note: tipsy means drunk and unsteady, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Boozy sponge desserts are going for next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipsy cakes' looks like the dessert; 'tipsy' is the anagram signal and 'go for a song' hides the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known Christian hymn, so it is an example of a song.

clue.text: On air, where did we witness the World Cup build-up coming to a head?

indicators.note: on air means broadcast, so the word is spoken out rather than spelt

parts.words: where did we witness the World Cup
parts.note: the 2022 football World Cup was held in Qatar

explanation.surface: A broadcaster asking where viewers watched the run-up to the World Cup reach its climax.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue set in 2022: 'On air' says QATAR is spoken, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Catarrh is mucus that accumulates in the nose and sinuses, a build-up in the head.

clue.text: Fairly rebutted these facts

indicators.note: rebutted suggests turned back, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: fairly can mean slightly, a tad

explanation.surface: Someone politely rejected these claims.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for reference or analysis, a plural noun like 'these facts'.

clue.text: Where Phoenix is risen? Old stories about it

indicators.note: the anecdotes go about the other letters, wrapping round them

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories about a person
riz is an old or American dialect past participle of rise

explanation.surface: Plays on the myth of the phoenix rising again, told in old tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phoenix is risen' looks like the bird reborn, but Phoenix is the city and 'risen' gives RIZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenix is the state capital of this southwestern US state.

clue.text: Enough time to embrace love in court?

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer in its arms, hidden inside its letters

explanation.surface: Asks whether a lovers' kiss in a courtroom lasted long enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' is a tennis court, where love means zero.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring, love stands for a score of zero, another word for nothing at all.

clue.text: The risks people take involving the press

definitions.text: The risks people take involving the press

parts.words: The risks people take involving the press
parts.note: reads as journalists' dangers, but 'press' is pressing clothes with a hot iron in dangerous places

explanation.surface: Hints at the dangers people face dealing with journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: A real stunt sport in which people iron clothes on mountains or underwater, taking risks while pressing garments.

clue.text: See 21
Starts being 18 with this logical circuit?

parts.note: the answer, read as an instruction, is applied to the word Starts; what remains means the same as 18 across, DATA

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced puzzle about a circuit kicking off.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as the instruction 'no R', and it turns STARTS into STATS, synonym of 18 across (DATA).
explanation.definitionFit: A NOR gate is an electronic logic gate giving true only when every input is false.

clue.text: As correspondents are doing business — remotely placed?

definitions.meaning: letter-writers do their business by mail, trading by post
a store set up in a remote area for barter

explanation.definitionFit: A frontier store for barter in remote regions, and literally doing deals through the mail.

clue.text: Simple means to travel south via busy North Parade

indicators.note: the compass letter goes by way of, through, the scrambled letters
a busy street is bustling, so these letters are jostled into a new order

explanation.surface: Directions for a trip southward along a crowded street called North Parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' rearranges NORTH PARADE to HOREANDTRAP; 'via' puts S inside after HOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse pulling a light two-wheeled cart is an old-fashioned, basic way of getting around.
